route: 1 (published reliability/loadings, PLOS Table 2) + 8 (semantic coherence of means/SDs)
evidence: All numbers from verify_lunacortes_2019_social_value.R (VERDICT: PASS), live irw_fetch of a 1,332-row table x the S1 File XLSX, N=444. Code derivation is not at issue and was checked anyway: data/lunacortes_2019_vsn_scales.py lowercases 'Social-Val1'..'Social-Val3' and melts by name, and all three live columns are cell-for-cell identical to their namesake source columns (444/444, 3/3 items). What was inferred is bullet-to-number, and the decisive number is Table 2's Cronbach's alpha of 0.822 for a Perceived Social Value factor that Table 2 shows with only TWO indicators, PSV1 (load 0.83) and PSV2 (0.84), because section 3.4 says PSV3 'presented factor loadings lower than the rest of the items' and was removed on the Lagrange test. Observed pairwise alphas: {social_val1,social_val2}=0.8219 (|diff| 0.0001), {social_val1,social_val3}=0.3447 (|diff| 0.4773), {social_val2,social_val3}=0.4576 (|diff| 0.3644); all three items together 0.6835. Only one pair is within 0.1 of the published value, so social_val3 is the paper's PSV3. Corroborated two ways: social_val3 has by far the weakest corrected item-total r, 0.2792 against 0.5912 (social_val1) and 0.6643 (social_val2); and it has the highest mean (5.383 vs 4.556 and 4.698) and smallest SD (1.316 vs 1.590 and 1.597), which matches bullet 3, 'This tourism experience makes a good impression on other people', being the easiest to endorse and the semantic odd one out (about others' impression, not the respondent's own social standing, unlike bullets 1 and 2). DOES NOT ESTABLISH: social_val1 vs social_val2. The paper's published loadings for those two are 0.83 and 0.84 with an IDENTICAL robust t of 24.100, a gap too small to key on, and no other published per-item statistic separates them, so their assignment rests on Table 1 bullet order alone. The route therefore distinguishes one item of three from the other two, not every item from every other -- PARTIAL, not VERIFIED.
